at_sea: PROVED and pushed: a-refused-ask-leaves-a-row. domain.resolve() wrote its inference_calls row only AFTER resolver(request) returned, so every raise left the store untouched and the refusal rate of the system's ONLY inference door was unreadable. Now every raise escaping resolver(request) lands verdict='refused', answer NULL, cost 0, provenance naming the exception type and its message. THE PREDICATE CHANGED DURING THE BUILD and hypothesis 1 was KILLED by its own falsifier: the chart planned to sort host.py's error classes by whether a byte had been sent, and that is unavailable — domain.py imports NO host (the resolver is INJECTED, which is the module's design), and route.RouteRefused is a SIXTH reachable class that is pre-dispatch but a RuntimeError exactly like the four post-dispatch Host* ones, so no type test separates them. The line is the try: block. Hypothesis 5 was killed too, on one word of its own falsifier ('a new module-level import' — `import sys`, so a store failure while recording is loud on stderr instead of impersonating a host failure). 11 -> 14 teeth beside the domain, 11 new beside the probe, both green twice and sealed under netns; the row tooth was measured RED on unmodified HEAD ('found 0'). LIVE FIRE landed the first refused row this system has ever recorded (2026-08-18T01:28:54, HostUnreachable against 127.0.0.1:1), and a routed generate to hex answered at cost 15 in the same breath. The PROVED crossing went through the harbor's clearance gate, which correctly refused the first attempt: the seal's horizon had closed because the WATCHME crossing moved the component's fingerprint. Re-sealed, then cleared. THE CHART'S SCORE, MEASURED: 64 tool calls between the validate berth and done.
